text:
If your Sunday plans are outdoors, keep the jacket and umbrella close. Rain arrives this morning and hangs around through much of the day, occasionally coming down moderately, with a high only near 58. The forecast is a little split on how chilly it gets, but I’d plan for the cooler side of the 50s, especially with a south wind gusting to 25 mph. A quarter to half-inch of rain is possible before it pulls away this evening. On the lake, south winds around 10 to 20 knots and waves up to 3 feet make for a rough outing.

Tomorrow stays mostly cloudy early, then should brighten some, with a high near 61 and a north wind. That wind will be stronger on the water, 15 to 25 knots at first, with waves building to 3 feet. Plan on a dry Monday on land, but stay off the broad lake until the wind eases.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - Tonight will be chilly, but not as cold as last night. Lows will be in the 40s, but increasing clouds will put a cap on how cold it gets. These clouds are with a low pressure system to our southwest which will bring light rain to southern parts of the region by daybreak on Sunday. The rest of the day will be rainy, coming down moderately at times. This will be a beneficial rain with no significant impacts. However, it will be raw with highs in the 50s, so an umbrella and jacket are recommended if you plan to travel or be outdoors. A half inch or more of rain is possible by early evening. The rain will quickly move out during the evening with partly cloudy skies overnight.
